reason: 'Gregarious' means growing in groups. It describes plants, not a part. 'Aggregated' (clustered) is close but not the same, so a rule is risky.
Sheath-like means forming a sheath, which is sheathing.
Claviform is a synonym of clavate (club-shaped).
Beakless means without a beak, which is not beaked.
Indumented means having an indumentum (hair covering). Presence is right, but it depends on the indumentum bearer being released.
Bicolored means exactly two colours. 'Multi-colored' loses the 'two'. Use it only if there is no bicolored class.
Heteromorphic means two or more different forms. Dimorphic means exactly two. Use polymorphic or a rule with a constraint, not dimorphic.
Epigeal describes germination with cotyledons raised above ground. It is not the same as 'aerial' (borne in the air).
Lorate means strap-shaped.
Shaggy means long, soft, tangled hairs. Villous means long, soft, unmatted hairs. They are similar but the 'tangled' part is lost.
Ample means large or spacious. It is fine for broad organs, but 'increased size' is not clearly meant for every part.
Cracked can describe bark or soil surface cracks, not only fissures. For bark it fits, for other parts it is unclear.
Widening is a process. 'Dilated' means already widened. Map it only with a bearer constraint, if at all.
Coroniform means crown-shaped.
Maculate means spotted or blotched.
Corrugate means folded in ridges and furrows. Rugose means wrinkled. They are close but not the same.
Not visible means hidden or absent from view, not small. 'Inconspicuous' means hard to notice, which is weaker.
Buff is a pale yellowish brown, not orange yellow.
Crooked means bent.
Bluntly acute is a slightly less sharp acute, which is subacute.
Densely arranged means crowded.
Planar means flat.
Tridentate means three-toothed. Tricuspidate means three-pointed. They are similar but the teeth and cusps differ.
Not enlarged is the negation of increased size.
Produced means extended or drawn out (for example, a leaf produced into a tip). Excurrent means the axis runs through the apex. Not the same.
Carunculate means having a caruncle.
Ramiflorous means flowers on branches. Cauliflorous means flowers on the trunk. They are different.
Narrowly rounded is a kind of rounded apex, not blunt. Blunt is a different shape.
Unspotted means not spotted.
The word 'sparsely' (hair density) is lost. Use pubescent with a density value or leave it unmapped.
Apical means at the tip. For leaf and fruit parts it can mean the apex region, not the terminal position.
As an adjective, 'aggregate' fits clustered parts. It also names a fruit type (aggregate fruit), so the meaning changes by part.
Erect-spreading means erect and spreading together. Semi erect is a different, partly upright state.
Pulpy means soft and fleshy.
'Rooted' means bearing roots. Shoot-borne roots fit stems at nodes. It should not apply to a plant or a root.
Homostylous means all flowers have the same style length, which is not heterostylous.
Excavated means hollowed out, which is concave.
Echinulate means with small spines or prickles. 'Spiny' loses the small size.
Sclerified means thickened by sclerenchyma. Hard is only the result. It also changes the tissue meaning.
Verrucate means warty.
Abruptly acute is still an acute apex.
Narrowly acute is still an acute apex.
Tubercled means having tubercles, which is tuberculate.
Unequal-sided means asymmetrical, as in leaf bases.
Chaffy means covered in chaff-like scales or paleae. Scarious means thin and dry. They are different.
Dehiscing is the same as dehiscent.
Corrugated means folded in ridges and furrows. Rugose means wrinkled. They are close but not the same.
Funnel-form means funnel-shaped.
Curved-ascending means curved and then ascending. Ascending alone loses the curve.
Reclining means leaning or resting on a support, not decumbent (lying on the ground with tips turned up).
